- **[CARD-CLAIM]** — the filing seat's or triage's reading, relayed verbatim. ⛔ Re-measure before you build on it.

### 1. The defect

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.tsx` contradicts itself inside one component:

```tsx
:242  export const RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS = ['record', 'previous'];   // what a record-scoped mount OFFERS
…
:566            placeholder="record.status != 'done' && user.isAdmin" // what EVERY mount TEACHES
```

The placeholder is a **string literal**. It is ⛔ not parameterised by `scope`, so a record-scoped mount — where PR objectui#9854 deliberately stopped offering `user` — still teaches `user.isAdmin` three hundred lines away.

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** Control: the file has exactly **three** `placeholder=` sites. The other two are `:618` (`field / context`, a `SelectValue`) and `:642` (`value`, an `Input`) — both unrelated. ⇒ `:566` is the only CEL example, so this is one line's decision and not a family of them.

### 2. ⭐ The reading that makes it more than "an unoffered root" — ⛔ and you must re-take it

**[CARD-CLAIM]** The filing seat read objectstack `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts:253`–`:268` on `07c6f82` and reports that a condition formula is evaluated against **two bindings only** — `record` (via `pickRecordPayload`) and `previous` (via `pickPreviousPayload`). ⇒ no `user`, no `org`: at a server-evaluated mount the taught root is **unbound**, not merely unadvertised.

**[CARD-CLAIM]** Triage corroborated it from objectui's own side — `conditionScope.ts:83-120`'s comment, which it reports says the rule validator evaluates with `{ record, previous }` and **only** those, and that an unevaluable predicate is **fail-CLOSED**.

⛔ This seat re-measured **neither**. Both are the load-bearing facts of the card, so re-measure both on your base before you write a line of the fix — and if either fails to reproduce, that is a stop-and-report, not something to work around. The objectui one is in this repo and costs you nothing.

**[CARD-CLAIM]** Counter-fact from the objectui#9855 dev, also unverified here: `user` **is** in the engine's `SCOPE_ROOTS`, lints `ok:true`, and **is** bound by `buildExpressionScope` at every **client-evaluated** mount. ⇒ ⛔ `user.isAdmin` is not wrong everywhere. It is right at some mounts and unbound at others, which is precisely what one literal cannot express.

### 3. What to decide, and what must back it

The card deliberately does ⛔ not prescribe the shape. Three routes were named; pick one and justify it from readings:

- **A** — parameterise the placeholder by `scope`, reusing the `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS` machinery already in the file.
- **B** — derive the example from the mount's own declared subjects, so it cannot drift from what is offered.
- **C** — drop the second clause, leaving `record.status != 'done'`.

⭐ The bar: whichever you take, the end state must make it **impossible for the placeholder to teach a root the same mount does not offer** — without a second hand-maintained list, because a second list is how these three doors got out of step in the first place. If your route leaves the placeholder and the root set as two independently-edited literals, say so in the PR and say why that is acceptable.

### 4. Tests

⭐ A pin that cannot fail is worse than none. The assertion must break if someone re-hard-codes the placeholder, so ⛔ do not assert the literal string. Assert the **relation**: at a record-scoped mount, every root token the placeholder mentions is a member of the offered set.

Controls in the same body, or it is not a reading:
- subject — a record-scoped mount: the placeholder mentions no root outside `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS`;
- control A (the instrument must be able to FAIL) — feed the assertion the old literal and show it rejects it;
- control B (must stay unchanged) — a client-evaluated mount still offers what it offered before; ⛔ this card removes no capability there.

### 5. Scope fence

⛔ **objectui#9953** — the polymorphic `ConditionWidget` mount — is a **different subject**, not this card at a second site. Triage named the two apart and this seat adopted that: fixing one does not fix the other. ⛔ Do not touch it.
⛔ **objectui#9645 / objectui#9855** are landed. ⛔ Do not re-open, re-word or "tidy" what they did.
⛔ The engine's `SCOPE_ROOTS`, `buildExpressionScope`, and anything in objectstack are outside this face. If the right fix needs them, that is a stop-and-report.

Declared file face:

```
packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.tsx
packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/__tests__/**
.changeset/*
```

### 6. Stop conditions — a stop with evidence is a good outcome

- Either [CARD-CLAIM] in §2 fails to reproduce on your base ⇒ stop and report with the lines you read.
- The fix cannot be done without changing which roots a mount offers ⇒ stop; that is a capability change and ⛔ not yours.
- You find the placeholder is already parameterised on your base ⇒ stop, report what landed and when.

### 7. Deliverable

Branch, code, tests, changeset, push, **draft** PR with `Fixes #9952`. ⛔ Do not flip out of draft, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not merge — landing is this seat's act after review. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Report back as structured JSON.

In the PR body: the re-taken line numbers (⛔ not the card's), the route you chose from §3 with its justification, and the failing-control evidence from §4.

## Seat review — ACCEPT. PR objectui#9985 lands when CI converges.

Seat `domain:ui#2`, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`, 2026-09-19T02:05Z. Dev report `5738453649`, `status: "done"`, `open_questions: []`.

### 1. ⭐ Routes A and B collapsed, and that is the answer the bar demanded

The dispatch's bar was: make it **impossible** for the placeholder to teach a root the mount does not offer, **without a second hand-maintained list** — 「a second list is how these three doors got out of step」. The diff does not choose between A (parameterise by scope) and B (derive from the mount's subjects); it shows they are the same thing once the offered set is read once:

```tsx
const offeredRoots = roots ?? (scope === 'record' ? RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS : undefined);
…
placeholder={celExampleForRoots(offeredRoots)}
roots={offeredRoots}
```

⭐ The expression hoisted into `offeredRoots` is **byte-identical** to what the `roots` prop already carried, so the autocomplete's behaviour is provably unmoved — the change is that a second control now answers to the same value instead of to a literal.

And there is no second list. `CEL_EXAMPLE_CLAUSES` holds clauses, ⛔ not clause→roots pairs; `celRootsMentioned` reads each clause's roots **back out of its own text**, so a clause cannot claim a root it does not spell:

```ts
const clauses = offered
  ? CEL_EXAMPLE_CLAUSES.filter((c) => celRootsMentioned(c).every((r) => offered.includes(r)))
  : [...CEL_EXAMPLE_CLAUSES];
```

### 2. What this seat checked on the diff, and what each check answers

| the fence the dispatch set | how the diff satisfies it |
|:--|:--|
| ⛔ no capability may be removed at a client-evaluated mount | `undefined` forwards no narrowing and every clause survives ⇒ that placeholder is what it always was, byte for byte. Stated in the docblock and pinned as control B |
| ⛔ no second hand-maintained list | `celRootsMentioned` derives; there is nothing to keep in step |
| the pin must assert a RELATION, ⛔ not the literal | `celRootsMentioned` is exported **for that reason**, and its docblock says so: 「A pin that asserted the literal could not fail on the day someone re-hard-codes one」 |
| ⛔ the engine's `SCOPE_ROOTS` / `buildExpressionScope` / objectstack are outside the face | untouched; file list is 3 paths, all inside the declared face |

⭐ Two details this seat singles out because a weaker implementation would have missed them:

- **String literals are stripped before roots are read.** A quoted `'record.status'` is TEXT, and counting it as a reference is a silently-false predicate. The docblock names the prior card that fixed the same mistake elsewhere.
- **`CEL_WORD_LITERALS` excludes `true`/`false`/`null`/`in`** — word-shaped literals that a bare identifier scan would have read as unoffered roots and used to delete a correct clause.

### 3. The reverse verification is what makes this review cheap

Ablation, one-shot, committed-fix-first, source-resolved (the pin imports `./ConditionBuilder` relatively, so no `dist` sits between mutation and run). Mutation proven **on disk**, ⛔ not assumed: injected-text count 0 → 1, deleted-text count 1 → 0, HEAD blob `87a5b91b…` → `76f2e741…`. Direction declared **before** the run as 「turns RED」; observed `Tests 2 failed | 11 passed (13)`, the two being 「mentions no root outside `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS`」 (`expected [ 'user' ] to deeply equal []`) and 「shows something the OLD literal was not」. Restore proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, ⛔ never by an exit code; restored run `Tests 13 passed (13)`.

⭐ And the in-body failing control the dispatch required is present: the OLD literal is fed to the same relation and must be rejected **naming `user`**, with a companion case that an all-offered example is **accepted** — so it is ⛔ not a rejector that rejects everything.

### 4. Both relayed claims reproduced, and one citation corrected

The dispatch marked two facts **[CARD-CLAIM]** and ordered them re-measured. Both reproduce: objectstack's `wrapDeclarativeHook` docblock (condition evaluated against `record` and `previous`), and objectui's own `conditionScope.ts` (`{ record, previous }` and nothing else, fail-CLOSED). The counter-fact also reproduces — `introspectScope` advertises `user` at both `record` and `flattened` scope — so ⛔ nothing was declared wrong everywhere, which was the trap.

⚠️ One correction the dev found and this seat records rather than repairs: triage's citation 「`conditionScope.ts:83-120`」 does **not** frame what it quotes on today's tip — the two sentences sit in the file's top ruling list and in the `validation` key's own docblock, while `:83-120` opens at the `CONDITION_SCOPE_BY_METADATA_TYPE` declaration and covers only the second. Substance unaffected and reproduces in full. It is a GitHub comment, ⛔ not a tree file, so there is nothing to repair and nothing to file.

The dev measured the other three `CelPredicateField` mounts for the same shape (an independently-edited literal placeholder beside an independently-edited roots list) and found the shape present but **no live violation**: `ConditionalFormattingEditor`'s example against `ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS`, `ObjectFieldInspector`'s two against `FORMULA_ROOTS` and `FIELD_RULE_ROOTS`, and `PermissionAdvancedFacets`' RLS example, which declares no roots and so inherits the engine's advertisement carrying `current_user`. ⇒ unexercised drift, ⛔ not a measured defect ⇒ ⛔ correctly not a card. `celExampleForRoots` is now available to the next door in this family (objectui#9953) if that seat wants the shape closed.
